pr_title: feat(rust, python): automatically infer iso8601-like dates

issue_context.title: Inconsistent Date Parsing in `read_csv`
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

# Examples

```python
import polars as pl
import io

csv_text = """
YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY/MM/DD,YYYY.MM.DD,DD-MM-YYYY,DD/MM/YYYY,DD.MM.YYYY,MM-DD-YYYY,MM/DD/YYYY,MM.DD.YYYY
2023-01-01,2023/01/01,2023.01.01,01-01-2023,01/01/2023,01.01.2023,01-01-2023,01/01/2023,01.01.2023
"""
csv_data = io.StringIO(csv_text)
pl.read_csv(csv_data, try_parse_dates=True)
┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────────┬────────────┐
│ YYYY-MM- ┆ YYYY/MM/ ┆ YYYY.MM. ┆ DD-MM-YY ┆ ... ┆ DD.MM.YY ┆ MM-DD-YY ┆ MM/DD/YYYY  ┆ MM.DD.YYYY │
│ DD       ┆ DD       ┆ DD       ┆ YY       ┆     ┆ YY       ┆ YY       ┆ ---         ┆ ---        │
│ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆     ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ str         ┆ str        │
│ date     ┆ datetime ┆ str      ┆ date     ┆     ┆ str      ┆ date     ┆             ┆            │
│          ┆ [μs]     ┆          ┆          ┆     ┆          ┆          ┆             ┆            │
╞══════════╪══════════╪══════════╪══════════╪═════╪══════════╪══════════╪═════════════╪════════════╡
│ 2023-01- ┆ 2023-01- ┆ 2023.01. ┆ 2023-01- ┆ ... ┆ 01.01.20 ┆ 2023-01- ┆ 01/01/2023  ┆ 01.01.2023 │
│ 01       ┆ 01       ┆ 01       ┆ 01       ┆     ┆ 23       ┆ 01       ┆             ┆            │
│          ┆ 00:00:00 ┆          ┆          ┆     ┆          ┆          ┆             ┆            │
└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────────────┴────────────┘
```

# Problems

- the same format (`YYYY<sep>MM<sep>DD`) is interpreted differently for each separator (`-`, `/`, `.`)
    - `-`: date
    - `/`: datetime
    - `.`: str
- some dates are parsed while others are not, seems random and should be documented imo which formats are parsed and which are not because it's not obvious


# Solutions

- always parse as date if no time is given and don't parse as datetime
- clearly document which formats are parsed and which are not to avoid surprises

# Optional Additions

- add `date_format`/`date_fmt` parameter to `pl.read_csv` to allow users to specify the format
- Examples:
    - `pl.read_csv(csv_data, try_parse_dates=True, date_format="%Y-%m-%d")` # one format for all dates
    - `pl.read_csv(csv_data, try_parse_dates=True, date_format={"colA": "%Y-%m-%d", "colB": "%m-%d-%Y"})` # different formats for different columns

```python
Out[2]:
{'YYYY-MM-DD': Date,
 'YYYY/MM/DD': Date,
 'YYYY.MM.DD': Utf8,
 'DD-MM-YYYY': Date,
 'DD/MM/YYYY': Date,
 'DD.MM.YYYY': Utf8,
 'MM-DD-YYYY': Date,
 'MM/DD/YYYY': Date,

```

As the docs say:

>  Most ISO8601-like time zone naive formats can
> be inferred, as well as a handful of others.

So, not all formats can be inferred - that would probably be a never-ending process
